EPST.description: Static Earth Pressure (EPST). DIR selects XY (uses ANGLE) vs NORMAL (uses IN_PT), and SEL_TYPE selects GRUP (uses LOADING_AREA_GROUP) vs ELEM (uses ELEM_TYPE with ELEM_LIST/NODE_LIST) to drive which fields apply.

LOADCASE.description: Static load case name. Must match an existing load case (STLD) name; validated at runtime.

DIR.description: Load direction. XY applies the pressure horizontally (uses ANGLE); NORMAL applies it normal to the surface (uses IN_PT). Case-insensitive.

ANGLE.description: [DIR=XY] Horizontal direction angle of the earth pressure.

IN_PT.description: [DIR=NORMAL] Inner reference point (x, y, z) used to orient the pressure normal to the surface.

SF.description: Scale factor applied to the earth pressure load.

EP_TYPE.description: Static earth pressure type. AT_REST or ACTIVE. Case-insensitive.

SOIL_PROP.description: Soil property (POSP) name. Must match an existing soil property; validated at runtime.

SEL_TYPE.description: Selection type for the loading area. GRUP uses a loading area group (LOADING_AREA_GROUP); ELEM uses explicitly selected elements/nodes (ELEM_TYPE, ELEM_LIST, NODE_LIST). Case-insensitive.

ELEM_TYPE.description: [SEL_TYPE=ELEM] Element type of the selected loading elements. FRAME applies loads to frame element nodes; PLANAR applies to planar element nodes. Each element in ELEM_LIST must match this type at runtime. Case-insensitive.

NODE_LIST.description: [SEL_TYPE=ELEM] Node numbers defining the loading area. Each node must exist; validated at runtime.

ELEM_LIST.description: [SEL_TYPE=ELEM] Element numbers defining the loading area. Each element must exist and match ELEM_TYPE; validated at runtime.

LOADING_AREA_GROUP.description: [SEL_TYPE=GRUP] Loading area group name. Must reference an existing loading area group with at least one loading area plane; validated at runtime.

PRES_PROFILE_ITEMS.description: Pressure profile: list of level vs. pressure entries describing the earth pressure distribution.

LEVEL.description: Elevation level of this profile point.
